emergencecapitalpartners-emergence-capit.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
emergencecapitalpartners-emergence-capit.description: ABOUT THE ROLE You'll work directly with our largest customers to solve their most critical problems – then ship the solutions yourself. This is a technical role with significant customer exposure, sitting at the intersection of engineering, product, and customer success. Forward Deployed Engineers are the bridge between what customers need and what the product can do. You'll spend time on-site or deeply embedded with customers, understanding their workflows, pain points, and requirements. Then you'll come back and build, shipping features, integrations, and customizations that unlock value. The best FDEs develop deep domain expertise and become trusted advisors to customers. This role is ideal for engineers who want customer exposure, founders whose companies didn't work out but want to stay close to the market, or anyone who believes great products come from deep customer understanding. You'll have more context on customer needs than almost anyone in the company, and you'll use that context to shape what we build. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Partner with enterprise customers to understand requirements, scope projects, and expand into new use cases - Build and ship features, integrations, and customizations that solve specific customer problems (you will probably write code for customer-specific integrations, proof of concepts, and implementations). - Own the full cycle from customer problem identification through technical solution to production deployment - Develop deep domain expertise in customer workflows, troubleshoot issues in customer environments, and become a trusted technical advisor - Translate customer feedback and requirements into product roadmap inputs and feature requests - Collaborate with sales and core engineering to help prioritize what matters most to revenue, improve workflows and systems, and ship larger product initiatives informed by customer needs - Create technical documentation, training materials, and implementation guides for customers - Support customer onboarding and ensure successful adoption of new features QUALIFICATIONS - 4+ years of software engineering experience with strong coding skills in Python, TypeScript, or similar - Experience in a customer-facing technical GTM role: FDE, solutions engineer, technical consultant, or similar - Ability to context-switch between building and selling, comfortable in both writing production-quality code and customer meetings - Strong communication skills with ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders - Experience with enterprise software, integrations, or building on top of existing customer systems - Comfort with ambiguity and ability to scope and execute projects with minimal direction - Track record of shipping production code and delivering measurable customer outcomes - Willingness to travel for customer engagements (typically 20-40%) NICE TO HAVE - Previous experience as an FDE at Palantir, solutions engineer at Scale AI, or similar customer-facing technical GTM role - Background as a technical founder or early startup engineer - Domain expertise in financial services, legal, healthcare, or other enterprise SaaS verticals - Experience with AI/ML systems, data pipelines, or analytics infrastructure - Consulting background with technical implementation experience - Experience at a company selling into enterprise customers with complex requirements

jobgether-jobgether:lever:ece6b318-dff6-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Lead Site Reliability Engineer - Imunify Reliability Platform based in New Zealand. This is a greenfield SRE leadership opportunity within a large-scale, security-focused product environment. You will define what “healthy” means across roughly 70 components spanning cloud services and customer-hosted agents. You will establish SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, monitoring standards, alerting, and escalation practices from the ground up. Your work will directly improve the ability to detect silent security-control degradation before it becomes a widespread customer-impacting issue. You will collaborate closely with engineering leads and senior engineers while building the telemetry and reliability platform yourself. The environment is remote-first, async, technically demanding, and focused on measurable outcomes rather than dashboards for their own sake. This is an opportunity to shape the reliability culture and foundations of a major security product. Define and establish meaningful SLIs for approximately 70 product components, working with squad leads and senior engineers to agree on ownership, measurement, tiering, SLOs, and error budgets. Develop a reliability taxonomy covering service availability and latency, fleet reachability and configuration convergence, security-control efficacy, artifact delivery, and telemetry pipeline health. Ensure reliability indicators are independently measurable and cannot be disabled by the same failure they are intended to detect. Design and build the telemetry collection pipeline for customer-hosted agents and cloud services, balancing push-based collection, sampling, privacy constraints, data quality, and cardinality. Extend instrumentation across Python, Go, and Rust components in collaboration with product engineering teams. Consolidate existing dashboards, queries, and reporting mechanisms into a smaller, more reliable observability platform, retiring tooling that does not provide meaningful operational value. Implement symptom-based, SLO-driven alerting with multi-window burn-rate principles and clear page, ticket, and dashboard classifications. Ensure every production alert has a defined owner, documented failure mode, and actionable runbook. Establish ongoing alert-quality practices, including periodic reviews, measurable actionable-alert rates, and deliberate removal of unnecessary alerts. Build a machine-readable ownership and escalation model that routes incidents to the appropriate engineering squads. Establish severity definitions, acknowledgement expectations, follow-the-sun escalation practices, and clean handoff procedures across multiple time zones. Strengthen incident command and blameless postmortem practices, including reliable timelines, ownership, and follow-through on corrective actions. Coach engineering squads to own their own operational responsibilities and paging rather than becoming a centralized buffer for other teams' alerts. Deliver measurable reliability outcomes over the first year, including complete SLI ownership, production telemetry, tiered alerting, squad on-call adoption, and a significant reduction in the time required to detect silent security-control degradation. Requirements Substantial production engineering or SRE experience, including experience defining and implementing an SLO framework rather than simply operating within an existing one. Strong Python skills and the ability to read and modify Go or Rust code when implementing instrumentation and reliability improvements. Strong hands-on experience with time-series and event telemetry at scale, including Prometheus/OpenMetrics, Grafana, Alertmanager-class routing systems, and columnar or high-cardinality data stores such as ClickHouse or equivalent technologies.
